newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Foreign investors eye Bulgaria domestic debt paper.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors eye Bulgaria domestic debt paper.

text.p: Foreign investors, eyeing high yields and pending privatisations, bought Bulgarian government securities worth 34 billion levs ($22.8 million) and $28 million between April 12-25, a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official said.

"This brought the total worth of domestic bad debt bonds and other government securities bought by foreigners in March and April to $128 million and around 81 billion levs," head of State Credits department at the BNB Nikolina Micheva told Reuters.

Interest of foreign investors in local debt paper was running high, Micheva said, as Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance improved and the interim cabinet moved towards speeding up sell-offs to raise desperately needed cash.

The interim government, in office since mid-February has brought monthly inflation for March down to 12.3 percent from 242.7 percent the month before and has reversed the lev fall from around 3,000 to the dollar to about 1,500 now.
The 81 billion levs were invested mainly in treasury paper with maturity of over six months as profits from only this type of government securities can be repatriated, said Micheva.
Under Bulgarian law foreigners can invest in Bulgarian government securities through resident foreign banks and local ones.
"High yields and the stable lev/dollar exchange rate have made the Bulgarian government securities market one of the most attractive ones to foreign investors," a commercial bank dealer said.

Yields on the last issues of six- and 12-month floater coupon T-bills auctioned on April 21 were 52.39 and 108.06 percent until maturity, respectively under the BNB main interest rate of 8.03 percent that was then in force.
Interest on the paper is pegged to the main interest rate and is adjusted every time the rate is changed by the BNB.
Now the main interest rate is set at 6.20 percent monthly or 74.40 percent annually. This compares with expectations of April monthly consumer price inflation below March's 12.3 percent.

Trade in domestic bad debt bonds, known as ZUNKs was also boosted by the cabinet's decision in April to raise the stake in local state small and medium-size firms that can be paid in with ZUNKs in sell-offs to 80 percent from 50 percent.
Both lev- and dollar-denominated ZUNKs are accepted as means of payment in sell-offs at par value while their minimum acceptable prices are now set at 35 and 45 percent of par, respectively.

Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88 ($ = 1494 Bulgarian Levs)
